text:
rachel (sales): Clara on the line for a POC. Their scripts started returning 401 then 403 for the same key. Can we triage quickly?

clara (customer): Hi all, using the SDK and direct curl. First got 401, then after retry got 403 with 'key expired' then 'bound to different org' sometimes. Very confusing.

tamir (sales-eng): Curious. 401 -> invalid/expired key. 403 messages vary: could be rotation in progress or header mismatch. Which key are you using?

clara (customer): Key: SK.POC.9ZXY. We rotate keys nightly in our infra but this was a new demo key.

marc (eng): auth-bot, inspect SK.POC.9ZXY please.

auth-bot: token-inspect: SK.POC.9ZXY -> status: active, bound_org: org-acme-77, scopes: [generate], created_at: 2025-01-10T08:12:01Z, expires_at: 2025-01-11T08:12:01Z, last_rotated: 2025-01-10T08:12:01Z

clara (customer): Huh, shows active. But our logs show our service rotated the key at 08:30 and swapped to a new env var. We might have mixed old and new keys during the demo run. Could that explain 401 then 403?

marc (eng): Yes. If you send an old key you'll get 401 (invalid/expired). 403 "bound to different org" happens if the header X-Project or X-Org points at a different tenant than the key binding. Any chance you're setting X-Project in the SDK?

clara (customer): Our demo harness sets X-Org header for multi-tenant routing. Example curl:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer SK.POC.9ZXY" -H "X-Org: org-acme-77" -H "X-Project: proj-88" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```

marc (eng): Can you try removing X-Project header and retry? X-Project might be scoped to a different org and cause the 403. Also check that the runtime updated env vars to the new key atomically.

clara (customer): Removing X-Project yields 200. OK that was it. But what's odd: sometimes we hit a rate-limit shortly after switching keys. Any relation?

ops (sre): Rate-limit is keyed by token or org depending on plan. If you rotate quickly and both old and new tokens hit the service, they each count. We saw a short burst at 08:31 of 120 req/min from your demo IP; that triggered small throttling for a minute. Not related to auth messages though.

rachel (sales): Clara, do you want us to issue a single-demo key that is project-agnostic so you don't have to set headers?

clara (customer): That would be great. Also procurement asked for pricing and a security contact.

finance-bot: Based on your expected demo traffic (500 requests over 30m), estimated hosted cost ~= $0.25. Enterprise pricing and contract contact: enterprise-sales@redwood.ai.

marc (eng): For internal follow-up: We should update the SDK docs to warn about X-Project vs X-Org mismatch causing 403 and add a short troubleshooting snippet. Small ticket created.

auth-bot: issued-temp-key: TK_DEMO_ACME scope: generate bound_org: org-acme-77 expires_in: 7200s

clara (customer): TK_DEMO_ACME works, thanks! Please also send SOC2 artifact links for procurement.

rachel (sales): I'll send pricing and SOC2 links, and loop in enterprise contact if they want dedicated capacity. Action items: 1) rachel send docs/pricing, 2) marc add SDK doc note, 3) ops to confirm rate-limit behavior in docs.

marc (eng): I'll file a docs PR and include a sample error log and quick fix.

rachel (sales): Thanks team, closing this thread. Clara, feel free to reopen if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
